name: Tuomo Suntola
summary: Finnish inventor and pioneer of atomic layer deposition (ALD) and electroluminescent display technology.

name: Riikka L. Puurunen
summary: Materials scientist and historian who authored the retrospective essay on ALD history.

name: Helsinki University of Technology
summary: Finnish university where Suntola completed his master's and doctoral studies in electrical engineering.

name: VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland
summary: Finnish research institute where Suntola developed the Humicap humidity sensor.

name: Instrumentarium Oy
summary: Finnish medical instrumentation company where Suntola led an independent R&D group.

name: Lohja Oy
summary: Finnish building materials and electronics company that acquired Suntola's EL display project.

name: Microchemistry Ltd.
summary: Finnish company founded by Suntola to commercialize ALE technology for solar and catalysis applications.

name: ASM Microchemistry
summary: Dutch semiconductor equipment manufacturer that acquired Microchemistry Ltd.

name: Atomic Layer Epitaxy
summary: Thin-film growth technique invented by Suntola, later renamed atomic layer deposition.

name: Atomic Layer Deposition
summary: Modern name for the ALE thin-film growth technique, widely used in semiconductor manufacturing.

name: Humicap 1
summary: Capacitive humidity sensor developed by Suntola using thin polymer films.

name: F-120 Reactor
summary: First commercial ALD reactor designed by Suntola for photovoltaic research.

name: European SEMI Award 2004
summary: Prestigious industry award recognizing Suntola as a pioneer in atomic layer deposition.

name: Tampere
summary: City in Finland where Tuomo Suntola was born.

name: Espoo
summary: City in Finland where Suntola established his research labs and where VTT and Microchemistry were located.

name: San Diego
summary: City in California where Suntola first publicly presented ALE technology.

name: Boston
summary: City in Massachusetts where Suntola demonstrated ALE for semiconductor applications.

name: Munich
summary: City in Germany where Suntola received the European SEMI Award.

name: Leningrad
summary: City in the Soviet Union (now St. Petersburg) visited by Suntola to meet molecular layering inventors.

name: Thor Stubb
summary: Professor at HUT who supervised Suntola's doctoral research and assigned him the humidity sensor project.

name: Tapio Alvesalo
summary: Head of Neste Advanced Power Systems who suggested applying ALE to solar panels.

name: Sven Lindfors
summary: Close collaborator of Suntola in ALE reactor design and photovoltaic research.

name: Arto Pakkala
summary: Colleague who reacted to the successful demonstration of the ZnCl2/H2S ALE process.

name: Antti Piippo
summary: Business manager who reorganized Lohja's electronics division and later bought Elcoteq.

name: Ahti Aintila
summary: Developer of driving circuitries and fine-line PCB technology for ALE-EL displays.

name: Matti Ervasti
summary: Business-oriented managing director who took over Microchemistry from Suntola.

name: Jun-ichi Nishizawa
summary: Japanese professor who independently researched and promoted ALE/MLE in Japan.

name: Salah Bedair
summary: US professor who demonstrated ALE of GaAs at North Carolina State University.

name: Lauri Niinistö
summary: Finnish professor who co-operated with Suntola on ALE chemistry and organized early ALE conferences.

name: Victor Drozd
summary: Soviet scientist who invited Suntola to Leningrad to connect the ALE and molecular layering histories.

name: Aleskovskii
summary: Soviet professor who independently invented molecular layering in the 1960s.

name: Marina Lindblad
summary: Doctoral student who worked on ALE catalysts and quantum chemical analysis of ZnS growth.

name: Jaakko Hyvärinen
summary: Developer of the Quicksun solar simulator and founder of Endeas Oy.

name: Picosun Oy
summary: Finnish company founded by Lindfors and Poutiainen to manufacture ALE reactors.

name: Beneq Oy
summary: Finnish company that acquired Planar's EL plant and continues commercial ALE-EL production.

name: Fortum Oyj
summary: Finnish energy company where Suntola worked as a research fellow after Neste merged with IVO.

name: Planar Inc.
summary: American competitor that acquired Lohja's EL business in 1990.
